relationships.subject: GRK
relationships.evidence_quote: Many studies have demonstrated that phosphorylation of CB1R by GRKs and subsequent recruitment of β–arrestin2 play a critical role in the CB1R neuroadaptations responsible for cannabinoid tolerance.

relationships.subject: β-arrestin2
relationships.evidence_quote: cannabinoid agonists producing minimal β–arrestin2 signaling and recruitment, a protein involved in CB1R desensitization and downregulation, might produce less tolerance

relationships.subject: FAAH
relationships.evidence_quote: Hydrolysis of AEA occurs via fatty-acid amide hydrolase (FAAH)

relationships.subject: MAGL
relationships.evidence_quote: Breakdown of 2-AG is medicated predominately through the action of monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL; 85% of 2-AG breakdown)

key_findings: Review: cannabinoid tolerance arises from CB1R downregulation and desensitization mediated by GRKs, β-arrestin2, JNK and PKA.
No tolerance to CB2-selective agonists; AEA and 2-AG elicit minimal tolerance.
